newsitem.title: USA: Converse signs Rodman, to name shoe after star.
newsitem.headline: Converse signs Rodman, to name shoe after star.

text.p: Converse Inc. signed Chicago Bulls forward Dennis Rodman to a multiyear contract and will name a new basketball shoe after him, the company said Monday.
Rodman, a rebounding champion currently serving an 11-game suspension for kicking a courtside cameraman, will appear in commercials advertising Converse's All Star Springfield shoes, Converse said.
Rodman will wear the Springfield shoe until the playoffs, when Converse will launch its new Rodman shoe.
No details of the contract were provided.
"We look forward to Dennis' imminent return to the NBA and the world champion Chicago Bulls," James Solomon, Converse's senior vice president of marketing, said in a release.

Rodman was suspended by the National Basketball Association for at least 11 games, fined $25,000 and ordered to see a counsellor for kicking a courtside cameraman in Minneapolis two weeks ago. The player agreed to pay the cameraman $200,000 in an out-of-court settlement.
"This is going to be a good partnership since Converse and I will work closely together to create some unique products, for both my on-court game and for hanging out," Rodman said in a statement.

Known for his sometimes bizarre behaviour, multi-hued hair and many tattoos, Rodman has captured five consecutive NBA rebounding titles. Off the court, his autobiographical book, "Bad as I Wanna Be," has sold almost a million copies.
